mechanism_narrative: A sustained growth trend in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active as the labor market trend is consistently positive in the current economic cycle.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS has grown by 1.5% year-over-year in the last 12 months
failure_condition: When PAYEMS is growing (12-month YoY growth > 0.5%), the S&P 500 has negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:FEDFUNDS is at 0.07% as of 2021-03-01, but the threshold is 2.0%
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises above 2.0%, the S&P 500 has positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 3 months, the S&P 500 has positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST has declined by 2.5% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in HOUST does not lead to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns (i.e., returns are positive in >50% of such periods).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, the S&P 500 has positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is always active as consumer spending has been resilient in the current economic cycle.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS has grown by 3.0% year-over-year in the last 12 months
failure_condition: When RSAFS is growing (12-month YoY growth > 1.0%), the S&P 500 has negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in retail sales (RSAFS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a weakening consumer economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 1.0% YoY and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: When RSAFS falls > 1.0% YoY and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, the S&P 500 has positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises above 5.5%, the S&P 500 has positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.
